theory.title: Greetings
theory.text:
At the beginning of a conversation, it is useful to know a few basic phrases.

Здравей. — Hi.
Здравейте. — Hello.
Добро утро. — Good morning.
Добър ден. — Good afternoon.

theory.title: Introductions
theory.text:
In Lesson 1 we learn how to introduce ourselves and ask about the other person.

Как се казваш? — What is your name?
Аз съм Хасан. — I am Hasan.
Откъде сте? — Where are you from?
Аз съм от Сирия. — I am from Syria.

theory.title: Countries and Nationalities
theory.text:
It is useful to know how to name a country, a nationality, and a profession.

Аз съм от България. — I am from Bulgaria.
Тя е българка. — She is Bulgarian.
Той е бежанец. — He is a refugee.
Тя е учителка. — She is a teacher.

theory.title: Food and Drinks
theory.text:
Lesson 2 introduces basic vocabulary for food and drinks.

вода — water
чай — tea
кафе — coffee
хляб — bread
баница — banitsa

theory.title: What Is This
theory.text:
A simple pattern is used to name an object.

Какво е това? — What is this?
Това е баница. — This is banitsa.
Това е хляб. — This is bread.

theory.title: I Like and I Want
theory.text:
With food and drinks it is useful to practise simple wishes and preferences right away.

Аз обичам кафе. — I like coffee.
Аз не искам сок. — I do not want juice.
Искаш ли вода? — Do you want water?

theory.title: At the Restaurant
theory.text:
This lesson teaches short phrases for being seated and placing an order.

Свободно ли е? — Is it free?
Да, заповядайте. — Yes, come in.
Не, съжалявам, заето е. — No, sorry, it is occupied.

theory.title: Ordering
theory.text:
The main phrases in a restaurant are asking for a menu and ordering drinks or food.

Може ли едно меню? — Can I have a menu?
Едно кафе, моля. — One coffee, please.
Един айрян, моля. — One ayran, please.

theory.title: The Bill
theory.text:
It is useful to know how to finish an order politely.

Нещо за ядене? — Something to eat?
Може ли една супа? — Can I have a soup?
Може ли сметката? — Can I have the bill?

title: Lesson 4
subtitle: Shopping at the Supermarket and Market

theory.title: Products
theory.text:
This lesson expands shopping vocabulary.

домат — tomato
краставица — cucumber
ябълка — apple
лимон — lemon
пилешко месо — chicken meat

theory.title: Preferences
theory.text:
Shopping phrases are easy to connect with the verbs we already know.

Какви плодове обичате? — What fruit do you like?
Ябълки и портокали. — Apples and oranges.
Какво месо обичате? — What meat do you like?

theory.title: The Product You Need
theory.text:
The learner should be able to name a specific product and say what they want to buy.

Искам хляб. — I want bread.
Искам вода. — I want water.
Обичам чай. — I like tea.

theory.title: Places in the City
theory.text:
This lesson introduces the main places in a city.

аптека — pharmacy
банка — bank
библиотека — library
болница — hospital
музей — museum
поща — post office

theory.title: Where Is It Located
theory.text:
To ask for directions or explain a place, you often need the definite form of a noun. In Bulgarian it is added to the end of the word.

аптека → аптеката — pharmacy / the pharmacy
библиотека → библиотеката — library / the library
парк → паркът — park / the park
център → центъра — centre / the centre
Къде е аптеката? — Where is the pharmacy?
Библиотеката е в центъра. — The library is in the centre.
Паркът е до реката. — The park is by the river.

theory.title: Endings -ta, -ut, -to, -te
theory.text:
The ending depends on the gender and number of the word.

Feminine nouns usually take -ta: apteka -> aptekata, ulitsa -> ulitsata, reka -> rekata.

Masculine nouns often take -ut / -yat when the word is the main subject of the sentence: park -> parkut, hotel -> hotelut, tsentur -> tsenturut.

After prepositions in simple phrases, we often see the short form -a / -ya.

Neuter nouns take -to, and the plural takes -te: kino -> kinoto, myasto -> myastoto, magazini -> magazinite.

в центъра — in the centre
до площада — next to the square
до хотела — next to the hotel

theory.title: Address and Landmarks
theory.text:
It is also useful to know words for addresses and landmarks.

Живея на тази улица. — I live on this street.
Живея в този блок. — I live in this building block.
Хотелът е до площада. — The hotel is next to the square.

theory.title: Family Members
theory.text:
In this lesson we name family members and talk about relatives.

майка — mother
баща — father
брат — brother
сестра — sister
деца — children

theory.title: Do You Have a Family
theory.text:
Short questions and answers with imam / nyamam are very useful.

Имаш ли брат? — Do you have a brother?
Да, имам. — Yes, I do.
Не, нямам. — No, I do not.

theory.title: Short Possessive Forms
theory.text:
In Bulgarian, words such as my, your, his, and her often come after the noun in a short form.

ми — my / my / my
ти — your / your / your
му — his
ѝ — her
ни — our / our / our
ви — your / your / your
им — their
Това е баба ми. — This is my grandmother.
Къде е семейството ти? — Where is your family?
Жена му е учителка. — His wife is a teacher.
Мъжът ѝ е лекар. — Her husband is a doctor.
Децата ни са в България. — Our children are in Bulgaria.
Как се казва синът ви? — What is your son's name?
Синът им живее във Варна. — Their son lives in Varna.

theory.title: Counting People: dvama, trima, chetirima
theory.text:
Special counting forms are often used for men and mixed groups of people.

двама — two people / two men
трима — three people / three men
четирима — four people / four men
Имам двама братя. — I have two brothers.
Имам трима синове. — I have three sons.
Имам четирима внуци. — I have four grandsons.

theory.title: The Preposition na
theory.text:
The preposition na is very common. In Lesson 6 it appears in two important patterns.

1. Age: na + number + years

2. Family relationship: who is related to whom.

Синът ми е на десет години. — My son is ten years old.
Дъщеря ми е на осем години. — My daughter is eight years old.
На колко години си? — How old are you?
Саид е съпруг на Латифа. — Said is Latifa's husband.
Латифа е съпруга на Саид. — Latifa is Said's wife.
Джоана е внучка на Саид и Латифа. — Joana is the granddaughter of Said and Latifa.

theory.title: Describing Relatives
theory.text:
In this lesson we also describe people. The adjective changes with gender and number.

хубав мъж — a handsome man
хубава жена — a beautiful woman
хубаво дете — a beautiful child
хубави хора — beautiful people
Брат ми е висок. — My brother is tall.
Майка ми е ниска. — My mother is short.
Дядо ми е стар. — My grandfather is old.
Сестра ти е по-млада. — Your sister is younger.

theory.title: Weather
theory.text:
Lesson 7 teaches how to describe the weather with simple ready-made phrases.

Днес е топло. — It is warm today.
Днес е студено. — It is cold today.
Вали дъжд. — It is raining.
Вали сняг. — It is snowing.
Духа вятър. — It is windy.

theory.title: Days, Months and Seasons
theory.text:
For days of the week, the preposition v is usually used. If the next word also begins with v, the form vuv often appears.

For months, seasons, and a period within time, prez is often used.

В понеделник работя. — I work on Monday.
В сряда почивам. — I rest on Wednesday.
Във вторник уча. — I study on Tuesday.
През март времето е хубаво. — The weather is nice in March.
През зимата е студено. — It is cold in winter.
През деня работя. — I work during the day.

theory.title: From ... to ...
theory.text:
The pattern ot ... do ... shows the beginning and the end of a time span.

От понеделник до петък работя. — I work from Monday to Friday.
От девет до пет работя. — I work from nine to five.
От сутрин до вечер уча. — I study from morning to evening.
Температурата е от пет до десет градуса. — The temperature is from five to ten degrees.

theory.title: Do, Predi and Sled
theory.text:
Do shows a limit: until what time something happens.

Predi means before, and sled means after.

До утре. — Until tomorrow.
До обяд работя. — I work until noon.
До вечерта вали дъжд. — It rains until evening.
Преди работа пия кафе. — I drink coffee before work.
Преди дъжда има вятър. — There is wind before the rain.
След урока отивам вкъщи. — I go home after the lesson.
След дъжда има слънце. — There is sun after the rain.

theory.title: Clock Time
theory.text:
To ask the exact time, the fixed phrase Kolko e chasut? is used. Another common question is V kolko chasa ...?

Колко е часът? — What time is it?
Сега е два часа. — It is two o'clock now.
В колко часа започва урокът? — What time does the lesson start?
Урокът започва в осем часа. — The lesson starts at eight o'clock.

theory.title: This Item: tozi, tazi, tova, tezi
theory.text:
The demonstrative word depends on gender and number.

този панталон, този пуловер — masculine gender
тази риза, тази рокля — feminine gender
това яке, това палто — neuter gender
тези обувки, тези чорапи — plural

theory.title: The Color Agrees with the Clothing Item
theory.text:
The ending of the color changes together with the noun.

The same pattern is used with byal, cheren, cherven, zelen, zhult, and kafyav.

син панталон — blue trousers
синя риза — a blue shirt
синьо яке — a blue jacket
сини обувки — blue shoes

theory.title: The Verb Nosya - To Wear
theory.text:
Аз нося бяла риза. — I wear a white shirt.
Ти носиш черен панталон. — You wear black trousers.
Той / тя носи син пуловер. — He / she wears a blue sweater.
Ние носим бели ризи. — We wear white shirts.
Вие носите черни панталони. — You wear black trousers.
Те носят зелени пуловери. — They wear green sweaters.

theory.title: How to Say Dressed
theory.text:
The form oblechen agrees with the person.

Той е облечен с черен панталон. — He is dressed in black trousers.
Тя е облечена с червена рокля. — She is dressed in a red dress.
Детето е облечено с жълто яке. — The child is dressed in a yellow jacket.
Те са облечени със сини якета. — They are dressed in blue jackets.

theory.title: Specific Clothing: -iya, -ta, -to, -te
theory.text:
When we speak about a specific item, the color takes a definite ending.

Искам черния панталон. — I want the black trousers.
Искам синята риза. — I want the blue shirt.
Искам черното яке. — I want the black jacket.
Искам белите обувки. — I want the white shoes.

theory.title: Masculine: -iyat or -iya
theory.text:
In the masculine form, the ending depends on the role in the sentence.

The same model: siniyat pulover / iskam siniya pulover.

Черният панталон е нов. — The trousers are the subject, so we use -iyat.
Искам черния панталон. — The trousers are the object, so we use -iya.

theory.title: Home, Rooms and Furniture
theory.text:
къща — house; apartment; kitchen; bathroom; room; living room; bedroom; corridor
маса — table; chair; bed; sofa; wardrobe; lamp; carpet; shelf; mirror

theory.title: Comparison with po-
theory.text:
Po- means more and is written with a hyphen. The adjective agrees with the noun in gender and number.

Къщата е по-голяма. — The house is bigger.
Коридорът е по-дълъг. — The corridor is longer.
Леглото е по-удобно. — The bed is more comfortable.
Стаите са по-светли. — The rooms are brighter.

theory.title: Comparing Two Things: po-... ot ...
theory.text:
For direct comparison, the model po-... ot ... is used.

Къщата е по-голяма от апартамента. — The house is bigger than the apartment.
Кухнята е по-светла от коридора. — The kitchen is brighter than the corridor.
Диванът е по-удобен от стола. — The sofa is more comfortable than the chair.

theory.title: Choosing among All with nay-
theory.text:
Nay- means the most and is written with a hyphen.

Холът е най-голям. — The living room is the biggest.
Спалнята е най-тиха. — The bedroom is the quietest.
Леглото е най-удобно. — The bed is the most comfortable.

theory.title: How to Ask Questions
theory.text:
Кой диван е по-удобен? — Which sofa is more comfortable?
Коя стая е най-светла? — Which room is the brightest?
Кое легло е по-голямо? — Which bed is bigger?
Кои стаи са най-тихи? — Which rooms are the quietest?

theory.title: Main Verbs of Movement
theory.text:
In transport phrases it is important to distinguish the action.

тръгва — departs, starts the trip
заминава — leaves
спира — stops
пристига — arrives
пътувам — travel, go
връщам се — return
Автобусът тръгва. — The bus departs.
Влакът заминава. — The train leaves.
Автобусът спира. — The bus stops.
Влакът пристига. — The train arrives.

theory.title: Where from and Where to: ot / za
theory.text:
Ot shows the starting point: where the transport leaves from or where a person returns from.

Za shows the direction of the route: where the transport or person is headed.

A useful general model:

Автобусът тръгва от автогарата. — The bus leaves from the bus station.
Влакът заминава от Пловдив. — The train leaves from Plovdiv.
Връщам се от София. — I am returning from Sofia.
Автобусът тръгва за Сливен. — The bus leaves for Sliven.
Влакът заминава за Варна. — The train leaves for Varna.
Пътувам за Германия. — I am travelling to Germany.
Пътувам от София за Варна. — I travel from Sofia to Varna.

theory.title: Where It Stops or Arrives: v / na
theory.text:
V is usually used with a city, a country, or a part of a city.

Na is usually used with transport-related places: station, bus station, stop, airport.

Автобусът спира в центъра. — The bus stops in the centre.
Влакът пристига в София. — The train arrives in Sofia.
Самолетът пристига в България. — The plane arrives in Bulgaria.
Автобусът спира на автогарата. — The bus stops at the bus station.
Влакът пристига на гарата. — The train arrives at the station.
Самолетът пристига на летището. — The plane arrives at the airport.

theory.title: By What Means of Transport: s / sus
theory.text:
S shows what means of transport a person is using. Before some words, the form sus is used for easier pronunciation.

In one sentence you can combine transport and direction.

Question about transport:

Пътувам с автобус. — I travel by bus.
Пътувам с влак. — I travel by train.
Пътувам със самолет. — I travel by plane.
Пътувам с автобус за Варна. — I travel by bus to Varna.
С какво пътуваш? — How are you travelling?

theory.title: Returning: vrushtam se
theory.text:
The verb vrushtam se is used with the particle se.

Ot shows where a person returns from.

V shows where a person returns to.

Мустафа се връща от Враца. — Mustafa returns from Vratsa.
Тя се връща от гарата. — She returns from the station.
Мустафа се връща в Сирия. — Mustafa returns to Syria.
Връщам се в България. — I return to Bulgaria.
Откъде се връщаш? — Where are you returning from?
Къде се връщаш? — Where are you returning to?

theory.title: Morning and Basic Routine
theory.text:
Lesson 11 brings together everyday actions and times of day.

Сутрин се събуждам рано. — I wake up early in the morning.
Сутрин ставам рано. — I get up early in the morning.
Сутрин се мия. — I wash in the morning.
Сутрин се къпя. — I bathe in the morning.
Сутрин се обличам. — I get dressed in the morning.

theory.title: Work, Study and Home
theory.text:
Verbs often go together with a time phrase: sutrin, denem, sledobed, vecher.

Сутрин излизам от вкъщи. — I leave home in the morning.
Сутрин влизам в офиса. — I go into the office in the morning.
След закуска работя. — I work after breakfast.
След работа уча. — I study after work.
След работа се връщам вкъщи. — I return home after work.

theory.title: Everyday Actions
theory.text:
For an ordinary day, you need verbs such as do, take, give, sit down, cook, clean, and rest.

Сутрин правя закуска. — I make breakfast in the morning.
На обяд сядам на масата. — At lunch I sit down at the table.
На обяд вземам супа. — At lunch I take soup.
На обяд давам хляб. — At lunch I give bread.
На обяд готвя супа. — At lunch I cook soup.

theory.title: Evening and Free Time
theory.text:
In the evening we often describe simple actions at home and communication.

Вечер каня приятели. — In the evening I invite friends.
Вечер гледам филм. — In the evening I watch a film.
Вечер чета книга. — In the evening I read a book.
Вечер слушам музика. — In the evening I listen to music.
Вечер лягам рано. — In the evening I go to bed early.
Нощем спя добре. — At night I sleep well.

theory.title: Communication and Questions
theory.text:
Questions follow the familiar pattern with li or koga.

Polite commands:

За какво мислиш? — What are you thinking about?
Говориш ли български? — Do you speak Bulgarian?
Звъниш ли на майка си? — Do you call your mother?
Срещаш ли се с приятели? — Do you meet friends?
Вземете книгата. — Take the book.
Чакайте тук. — Wait here.
